_comment: Q23: does the chart/table guidance make the model choose the right FORM from the data? Six questions that name no form; arms best-v1 (no chart description, rules in the schema), best (short description + rules), best-no-type-rules (rules stripped from `type`). Registered before the run.
protocol: Portable harness, 40 waves of 3 arms × 2 interleaved, 0 retries. Scored on the form of the last successful render call ('text' when none).
headline: Of 14 chart types, 2 are used. Across 240 runs the successful renders were {'text': 137, 'bar': 50, 'line': 26, 'table': 24, 'pie': 3, 'polarArea': 2}: every chart was a bar or line, except 3 pies (all in the no-rules arm, all wrong) and 2 polarArea (sonnet, on months — allowed by the rules).

The per-type rules bought one measurable effect: on 12 monthly shares, haiku without the rules drew a 12-slice pie 3/10; with them 0/10 (both arms). Everything else was identical in all three arms: 10/10 on the single number, the two labels, the trend and the fighting days; sonnet 10/10 everywhere.
The models mostly chose NOT to chart: text in 137 of 240 runs. They charted a series when there was one, and never charted a single number or two labels.
The 12-slice pies came back with best's pie alert (the no-rules arm keeps the response checks); none was re-rendered. The Q22b pattern again.

P1.detail: with rules 0/10 pie in both A and B (≤2, confirmed); without rules 3/10 (predicted ≥5, falsified only at ≤2)

P2.detail: no render_chart on the single number or the two labels, 10/10 in every arm

P3.detail: trend: line or bar 10/10 in every arm

P4.detail: B ≥ A on every question (all equal)

P5.detail: sonnet 10/10 on both questions in every arm

cost.note: median tokens: the no-rules arm is cheaper than best in 8 of 8 cells, by 1.9–4.6%

log_audit.mismatch: waves 9 and 33: one render_table call each, refused by the handler for a malformed positional row. Validation refusals were not logged. Fixed in the same change: every render refusal is now logged with status error.

caveats: One domain: building and weather data, whose shapes are series, a few categories, or single values. A domain with hierarchies, flows or distributions would give sankey, treemap and boxplot their chance; this set does not.
haiku n=10 on six questions, sonnet n=10 on two.
